symptom: During the first minute of flight the vehicle was struck by two triggered lightning discharges (36.5 s and 52 s). Crew got master alarms, multiple caution/warning lights (three fuel-cell lights, AC bus light, fuel-cell disconnect, AC bus overload 1 and 2, Main Bus A and B out), a signal-conditioning-equipment (SCE) dropout that garbled telemetry, and loss/tumble of the inertial guidance platform.
documented_cause: Vehicle-triggered lightning as it passed through electric fields (special report, ref. 12). First strike's induced transient on the battery-relay bus exceeded the current rate-of-change limit of the SCRs in the fuel-cell overload sensors, disconnecting the fuel cells from the main buses; low bus voltage dropped out the SCE and tripped AC undervoltage. Second strike set high-order bits in the CDU, driving the Z-axis (yaw) middle-gimbal readout past 85 deg and down-moding the platform to coarse-align, causing the observed tumble. Nine SM instrumentation measurements permanently lost. Crew restored fuel-cell power to buses at 000:02:22. Anomaly closed; launch weather rules added for later missions.
